selection_rationale.purpose: Lists the explicit criteria (negative culture, low initial suspicion, reassuring clinical condition, reassuring CRP trends) required to stop antibiotics at 36 hours.
selection_rationale.source_text: For babies who are being treated with intravenous antibiotics because of risk factors for early-onset infection or clinical indicators of possible infection, stop antibiotics at 36 hours if: • the blood culture is negative and • the initial clinical suspicion of infection was not strong and • the baby's clinical condition is reassuring, with no clinical indicators of possible infection (see box 2 for clinical indicators of possible early-onset infection) and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration are reassuring. [2012, amended 2026]

selection_rationale.purpose: Describes the review process and factors to consider when antibiotics are continued beyond 36 hours despite a negative culture.
selection_rationale.source_text: When continuing intravenous antibiotics for longer than 36 hours despite negative blood cultures, review the need for ongoing antibiotics at least once every 24 hours, taking account of: • the level of initial clinical suspicion of infection and • the baby's clinical progress and current condition and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration. [2012] 1.22 Switching to oral antibiotics

selection_rationale.purpose: Provides guidance on switching from intravenous to oral antibiotics after 36 hours when initial suspicion was strong but criteria for stopping are not met.
selection_rationale.source_text: For babies born from 35+0 weeks' gestation with negative blood culture who need antibiotics for more than 36 hours because the initial clinical suspicion of infection was strong, consider switching treatment from intravenous to oral antibiotics at 36 hours or thereafter to complete the course (up to 7 days of antibiotics in total) if: • the baby's clinical condition is reassuring, with no current clinical indicators of ongoing infection (see box 2 for clinical indicators of possible early-onset neonatal infection) and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration are reassuring and • the baby is tolerating oral feeds. [2026]

selection_rationale.purpose: Outlines the risk‑factor and clinical‑indicator framework used to judge the strength of initial suspicion of infection.
selection_rationale.source_text: Use the following framework, based on the risk factors in box 1 and the clinical indicators in box 2, to make antibiotic management decisions as directed: • In babies with any red flag, or with 2 or more 'non-red-flag' risk factors or clinical indicators: － follow the recommendations in the section on investigations before starting antibiotics and － start antibiotic treatment according to the recommendations in this guideline and － do not wait for the test results before starting antibiotics • in babies without red flags and only 1 risk factor or 1 clinical indicator, use clinical judgement to decide: － whether it is safe to withhold antibiotics and － whether the baby's vital signs and clinical condition need to be monitored. If monitoring is needed, continue for at least 12 hours using a newborn early warning system • for babies without risk factors or clinical indicators of possible infection, continue routine postnatal care as covered in NICE's guideline on postnatal care. [2021]

selection_rationale.purpose: Emphasises the need for systems delivering blood‑culture results at 36 hours to enable timely stopping of therapy.
selection_rationale.source_text: Consider establishing hospital systems to provide blood culture results 36 hours after starting antibiotics for early-onset neonatal infection, to allow timely stopping of treatment and discharge from hospital. [2012]

selection_rationale.purpose: Warns against relying solely on CRP results for decisions about stopping antibiotics.
selection_rationale.source_text: Do not use C-reactive protein results alone to make decisions about starting, continuing or stopping antibiotics. [2026]

selection_rationale.purpose: Specifies that baseline CRP should be measured at start of therapy and used with subsequent trends to assess infection likelihood.
selection_rationale.source_text: Measure baseline C-reactive protein concentration when starting antibiotic treatment in babies who may have neonatal infection. Use this together with any subsequent readings to assess the likelihood of infection and response to treatment. [2021]

selection_rationale.purpose: Notes the usual 36‑hour interval for the second gentamicin dose, linking to the timing of the 36‑hour assessment point.
selection_rationale.source_text: If a second dose of gentamicin is given this should usually be 36 hours after the first dose (for criteria for stopping antibiotics at 36 hours, see recommendation 1.21.3 in the section on treatment duration for intravenous antibiotics for early- onset neonatal infection). Use a shorter interval if clinical judgement suggests this is needed, for example, if: • the baby appears very ill • the blood culture shows a Gram-negative infection. [2012]
